# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 79 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 79 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_079_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 2

**1** Among these the angel commanded crowns to be brought; and crowns were brought, of palm branches, and the angel crowned the men who had given back completely green rods, and he sent them away into the tower. **2** He also sent those whose rods were green and cracked into the tower, and he gave them seals. **3** All those who went into the tower were wearing the same clothing — white as snow. **4** He also sent away those who had returned half-green and half-withered rods, giving them clothing and seals. **5** As for those who gave back withered and moth-eaten rods — their standing was as apostates, as those who had betrayed the church and blasphemed the Lord through their shameful acts. Moreover they were ashamed of the name of the Lord by which they were called. These therefore completely perished. **6** But those whose rods were withered but not moth-eaten — these were hearers of the word but remained in their sins, not repenting. As for those who gave back their rods with a half-green and half-withered condition, they are those who are occupied with business and do not attach themselves to the saints; therefore half of them is living and half is dead. **7** But those who brought their rods two-thirds green and one-third withered are deniers; they denied many times. **8** Those who brought back their rods two-thirds withered and one-third green — these are men who believed, but for the most part they dwell in iniquity and wickedness, yet there is a certain portion of righteousness remaining in them. **9** Those who returned nearly all green rods — only the tip withered — these are those who believed truly and are faithful, but have slight stains. **10** And those who returned completely withered rods — these are those who have already apostasized and do not repent, and who will not repent on account of the hardness of their heart. Therefore the spirit of the Lord departed from them.

---

*EMET notes: the willow is explicitly identified in early Hermas commentary as the Law/Son of God. The ten categories of branch condition map to ten classes of believers.*
